p.src: Now Kuai Liang said, “Sun Jian is dead, and all his sons are still young. If we advance with all speed while they are weak and vulnerable, Jiangdong can be won with a single charge. But if we return the body and cease hostilities, allowing them time to recover their strength, they will become a menace to Jingzhou.” Liu Biao said, “Huang Zu is in their camp. How could I bear to abandon him?” Kuai Liang said, “What is wrong with sacrificing one witless Huang Zu to gain all of Jiangdong?” Liu Biao said, “Huang Zu is my trusted and intimate friend. It would be dishonorable to abandon him.” He therefore sent Huan Jie back to his camp with an agreement to exchange Sun Jian’s body for Huang Zu. Liu Biao recovered Huang Zu, while Sun Ce received his father’s coffin, ended the fighting, and returned to Jiangdong, where he buried his father on the plains of Qu’e. When the funeral rites were complete, Sun Ce led his army to Jiangdu. He recruited worthy men, welcomed scholars, humbled himself in dealing with others, and gradually attracted heroes from every quarter—but that need not detain our tale.

p.src: Meanwhile, in Chang’an, Dong Zhuo heard that Sun Jian was dead and declared, “One mortal threat to me has been removed!” He asked, “How old is his son?” Someone replied, “Seventeen.” Dong Zhuo gave the matter no further thought. From then on he grew still more arrogant and overbearing. Styling himself the “Venerable Father,” he usurped the imperial ceremonial retinue whenever he went abroad. He appointed his younger brother Dong Min General of the Left and Marquis of Hu, and his nephew Dong Huang Palace Attendant with overall command of the imperial guards. Every member of the Dong clan, young or old, was made a marquis. Two hundred and fifty li from Chang’an, he had the stronghold of Mei built, conscripting two hundred and fifty thousand laborers for the work. Its walls matched those of Chang’an exactly in height, depth, and thickness. Within stood palaces and storehouses stocked with twenty years’ provisions. He selected eight hundred young beauties from among the people and installed them there. Gold, jade, colored silks, and pearls were heaped up beyond reckoning. All his family lived inside. Dong Zhuo traveled back and forth to Chang’an, returning sometimes every fortnight and sometimes once a month; on each occasion, the highest ministers waited beyond Heng Gate to see him off.

p.src: Dong Zhuo often had a pavilion erected by the roadside, where he drank with the high ministers. One day, Dong Zhuo passed out through Heng Gate, and all the officials came to see him off. He detained them for a banquet. Just then, several hundred surrendered soldiers who had accepted amnesty in Beidi arrived. Dong Zhuo at once ordered that, before the assembled guests, some have their hands and feet cut off, some their eyes gouged out, some their tongues severed, and others be boiled in great cauldrons. Their wails shook the heavens. The officials trembled and dropped their chopsticks, while Dong Zhuo continued eating, drinking, talking, and laughing as calmly as ever. On another day, Dong Zhuo summoned all the officials to a grand banquet in the government hall, where they sat in two rows. After several rounds of wine, Lü Bu strode in and whispered a few words in Dong Zhuo’s ear. Dong Zhuo laughed and said, “So that is how it was.” He ordered Lü Bu to seize Minister of Works Zhang Wen at the feast and drag him from the hall. The officials turned pale. Before long, an attendant entered bearing Zhang Wen’s head on a red tray and presented it to Dong Zhuo. The officials were frightened out of their wits. Dong Zhuo laughed. “My lords, do not be alarmed. Zhang Wen conspired with Yuan Shu to do me harm. He had someone bring a secret letter, but it was mistakenly delivered to my son Fengxian, and so I had him beheaded. You gentlemen are innocent, so there is no need for fear.” The officials murmured their assent and dispersed.

p.src: Minister over the Masses Wang Yun returned to his residence. Brooding over what had happened at the banquet that day, he could not sit still. Late that night, beneath a bright moon, he took up his staff and walked into the rear garden. Standing beside a trellis of roses, he raised his eyes to heaven and wept. Suddenly he heard someone by the peony pavilion heaving sigh after sigh. Wang Yun crept closer and peered out. It was Diaochan, a singing girl of his household. She had been selected for his household as a child and taught song and dance. Now sixteen, she excelled alike in beauty and accomplishment, and Wang Yun treated her as his own daughter. Wang Yun listened for a long while, then shouted, “Wretch! Have you formed some secret attachment?” Startled, Diaochan fell to her knees and replied, “How would this lowly woman dare harbor a secret love?” Wang Yun said, “If you have none, why are you sighing so deeply in the middle of the night?” Diaochan said, “Permit me to speak what lies in my heart.” Wang Yun said, “Conceal nothing. Tell me the truth.” Diaochan said, “My lord, I owe you the kindness of raising me, teaching me song and dance, and treating me with every courtesy. Even if my body were ground to dust, I could not repay one ten-thousandth of your favor. Lately I have seen sorrow knotting your brows. I knew it must concern some grave affair of state, yet I dared not ask. Tonight I again saw that you could neither sit nor walk at ease, and so I sighed. I never imagined you would see me. If there is any use to which I may be put, I will not refuse though I die ten thousand deaths.” Striking the ground with his staff, Wang Yun cried, “Who would have thought the realm of Han should rest in your hands! Follow me into the painted chamber.”

p.src: Diaochan followed Wang Yun into the chamber. He ordered every maid and concubine out, seated Diaochan, and bowed before her, striking his head upon the floor. Diaochan fell to the floor in alarm. “My lord, why are you doing this?” Wang Yun said, “Take pity on the living people of the Great Han realm!” When he had spoken, tears gushed from his eyes like a spring. Diaochan said, “I have already told you: if you have any command for me, I will not refuse though I die ten thousand deaths.” Still kneeling, Wang Yun said, “The people are in mortal peril, and sovereign and ministers stand as precariously as a pile of eggs. None but you can save them. The traitorous minister Dong Zhuo intends to usurp the throne. Yet none among the civil and military officials at court can devise a plan against him. Dong Zhuo has an adopted son, Lü Bu, who is extraordinarily fierce and brave. I have observed that both men are slaves to lust. I therefore mean to use a chain stratagem: first I shall betroth you to Lü Bu, and afterward present you to Dong Zhuo. You must seize your opportunities between them, sow discord between father and son, and cause Lü Bu to kill Dong Zhuo, thus ending this great evil. The restoration of the imperial altars and the reestablishment of the realm will all be your achievement. What do you say?” Diaochan replied, “I promised you that I would not refuse though I die ten thousand deaths. Present me to them at once. I shall know what to do.” Wang Yun said, “If the affair is exposed, my entire household will be destroyed.” Diaochan said, “Do not worry, my lord. If I fail to repay this great cause, may I die beneath ten thousand blades.”

p.src: Wang Yun bowed his thanks. The next day he took several fine pearls from his family collection and had a skilled craftsman set them into a golden coronet, which he secretly sent to Lü Bu. Lü Bu was delighted and went in person to Wang Yun’s residence to thank him. Wang Yun prepared a sumptuous feast. When Lü Bu arrived, Wang Yun went out to welcome him, escorted him into the rear hall, and offered him the seat of honor. Lü Bu said, “I am merely a general in the Chancellor’s household, while you, Minister, are a great officer of the court. Why do you honor me so extravagantly?” Wang Yun replied, “There is no other hero in the realm today but you, General. I honor not your office, but your ability.” Lü Bu was overjoyed. Wang Yun pressed wine upon him with great courtesy and continually praised the virtues of Grand Tutor Dong and Lü Bu alike. Lü Bu laughed heartily and drank his fill. Wang Yun dismissed all the attendants, keeping only a few serving women to pour the wine. When they were half drunk, Wang Yun said, “Call my daughter here.” Presently, two blue-robed maids led Diaochan forth, gorgeously adorned. Lü Bu asked in astonishment who she was. Wang Yun said, “She is my daughter, Diaochan. You, General, have honored me with your affection and are as close as my own kin; therefore I have brought her to meet you.” He then ordered Diaochan to offer Lü Bu a cup of wine. Diaochan presented Lü Bu with wine, and the two exchanged amorous glances. Pretending to be drunk, Wang Yun said, “My daughter, entreat the General to drink a few cups deep. Our entire household depends upon him.” Lü Bu invited Diaochan to sit, but she made as if to withdraw. Wang Yun said, “The General is my dearest friend. What harm is there in your sitting with us?” Diaochan then sat beside Wang Yun. Lü Bu stared at her without once taking his eyes away. After several more cups, Wang Yun pointed to Diaochan and said to Lü Bu, “I wish to give this daughter to you as a concubine. Would you be willing to accept her?” Lü Bu left his seat and bowed his thanks. “If I may obtain such a bride, I shall serve you with the devotion of a dog or horse.” Wang Yun said, “I shall choose an auspicious day before long and send her to your residence.” Lü Bu was beside himself with joy and repeatedly glanced at Diaochan. Diaochan returned his affection with liquid glances. Soon the banquet ended. Wang Yun said, “I had wished to keep you here for the night, General, but I fear the Grand Tutor might become suspicious.” Lü Bu thanked him again and again with bows, then departed.

p.src: Several days later, Wang Yun saw Dong Zhuo at court. Taking advantage of Lü Bu’s absence from his side, he bowed to the ground and invited him: “I would ask the Imperial Preceptor to condescend to visit my humble home for a banquet. May I know whether this meets with Your Excellency’s pleasure?” Dong Zhuo said, “Since the Minister of the Interior invites me, I shall certainly hasten to attend.” Wang Yun bowed his thanks and returned home. He prepared every delicacy from land and water, placed the chief seat in the center of the front hall, spread brocade upon the floor, and hung curtains both within and without. At noon the next day, Dong Zhuo arrived. Wang Yun went out in full court dress to receive him, bowing twice and inquiring after his health. Dong Zhuo descended from his carriage. More than a hundred armored guards bearing halberds clustered about him as he entered the hall, then formed ranks on either side. Wang Yun bowed twice below the hall. Dong Zhuo ordered that he be helped up and granted him a seat at his side. Wang Yun said, “The Imperial Preceptor’s mighty virtue is so exalted that even Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou could not equal it.” Dong Zhuo was delighted. Wine was served and music played, while Wang Yun showed him the utmost deference. When evening fell and the wine had taken effect, Wang Yun invited Dong Zhuo into the rear hall. Dong Zhuo ordered the armored guards to withdraw. Holding up a cup, Wang Yun offered congratulations and said, “Since childhood I have made some study of the heavens. Observing the celestial signs by night, I find that the allotted span of the House of Han is exhausted. Your Excellency’s achievements and virtue resound throughout the realm. As Shun received the throne from Yao and Yu succeeded Shun, so would this accord perfectly with Heaven’s will and the people’s desire.” Dong Zhuo said, “How could I dare aspire to such a thing?” Wang Yun said, “Since ancient times, ‘those who possess the Way chastise those who lack it, and those without virtue yield to those who possess it.’ How could this be excessive?” Dong Zhuo laughed and said, “If the Mandate of Heaven truly comes to me, you, Minister, shall be the foremost among my founding ministers.” Wang Yun bowed his thanks. Painted candles were lit in the hall, and only maidservants remained to pour wine and serve the food. Wang Yun said, “The music of the imperial performers is unworthy of entertaining Your Excellency; but I happen to have a household performer whom I would venture to summon for your entertainment.” Dong Zhuo said, “Excellent.” Wang Yun ordered the latticed curtains lowered. Yesterday at court the Imperial Preceptor said to me, ‘I have a certain matter for which I must visit your home.’ I therefore made preparations and awaited the Imperial Preceptor. While drinking, he said, ‘I hear you have a daughter named Diaochan whom you have promised to my son Fengxian. I feared your word might not be firm, so I have come expressly to ask for her and to see her for myself.’ I dared not disobey, so I brought Diaochan out to bow before her future father-in-law. The Imperial Preceptor said, ‘Today is an auspicious day. I shall take this girl home at once and give her in marriage to Fengxian.’ Consider it, General: when the Imperial Preceptor had come in person, how could this old man dare refuse him?” Lü Bu said, “Forgive me, Minister. I misunderstood the situation in my haste. Tomorrow I shall come bearing thorns upon my back to beg forgiveness.” Wang Yun said, “My daughter has a modest dowry. Once she has been conveyed to the general’s residence, I shall send it after her.”

I misunderstood the situation in my haste. Tomorrow I shall come bearing thorns upon my back to beg forgiveness.”
Wang Yun said, “My daughter has a modest dowry. Once she has been conveyed to the general’s residence, I shall send it after her.”

p.src: Lü Bu thanked him and departed. The next day, Lü Bu made inquiries throughout the residence but heard no news at all. He went straight into the hall and questioned the concubines. One of them replied, “Last night the Imperial Preceptor slept with the new lady and has not yet risen.” Lü Bu was furious. He slipped behind Dong Zhuo’s bedchamber and peered inside. At that moment Diaochan had risen and was combing her hair by the window. Suddenly she saw reflected in the pond outside the window the figure of a very tall man wearing a warrior’s headdress over his bound hair. Stealing a glance, she saw that it was Lü Bu. Diaochan deliberately knitted her brows and assumed a sorrowful, unhappy expression, repeatedly wiping away tears with a fragrant silk kerchief. Lü Bu watched for a long time, then left. A short while later, he entered again. Dong Zhuo was already seated in the central hall. Seeing Lü Bu arrive, he asked, “Is all quiet outside?” Lü Bu replied, “Nothing is amiss.” He stood in attendance at Dong Zhuo’s side. As Dong Zhuo ate, Lü Bu stole glances around him. Within the embroidered curtain he saw a woman moving back and forth and peeping out, half her face faintly revealed, her eyes conveying affection. Lü Bu knew it was Diaochan, and his soul was sent adrift. Seeing Lü Bu in this state, Dong Zhuo grew suspicious and jealous. “Fengxian,” he said, “if you have no business here, withdraw.” Lü Bu went out in bitter dejection.

p.src: After taking Diaochan into his household, Dong Zhuo became so infatuated with her beauty that for more than a month he did not attend to affairs of state. Dong Zhuo happened to fall slightly ill. Diaochan scarcely loosened her garments as she attended him night and day, bending herself to his every wish, and his delight in her grew still greater. Lü Bu entered the inner apartments to inquire after his health and found Dong Zhuo asleep. Diaochan leaned half her body out from behind the bed and looked toward Lü Bu. She pointed first to her heart, then to Dong Zhuo, all the while shedding tears without cease. Lü Bu’s heart seemed to shatter. Through bleary eyes, Dong Zhuo saw Lü Bu staring fixedly behind the bed without once shifting his gaze. Turning to look, he saw Diaochan standing there. Dong Zhuo flew into a rage and berated Lü Bu: “How dare you make advances to my beloved concubine! Guards, drive him out! He is never again to enter this hall.” Lü Bu returned home in anger and resentment. On the road he happened to meet Li Ru and told him what had occurred. Li Ru hurried in to see Dong Zhuo and said, “Your Excellency seeks to gain the empire. Why rebuke the Marquis of Wen for so trifling an offense? Should his loyalty waver, the great enterprise will be lost.” Dong Zhuo asked, “What should I do?” Li Ru replied, “Tomorrow morning, summon him inside, bestow gold and silk upon him, and soothe him with kindly words. Then all will naturally be well.” Dong Zhuo followed his advice. The next day, he sent someone to summon Lü Bu into the hall and consoled him, saying, “The other day I was ill and my mind was confused. I spoke mistakenly and hurt you. Do not take it to heart.” He then bestowed upon him ten jin of gold and twenty bolts of brocade. Lü Bu thanked him and returned home; yet although his body remained at Dong Zhuo’s side, his heart was wholly fixed upon Diaochan.

p.src: Once Dong Zhuo had recovered from his illness, he entered the court to discuss affairs of state. Lü Bu followed him bearing his halberd. Seeing Dong Zhuo engaged in conversation with Emperor Xian, he seized the opportunity to carry his halberd out through the inner gate, mounted his horse, and rode straight to the Chancellor's residence. He tethered his horse before the residence, carried his halberd into the rear hall, and soon found Diaochan. Diaochan said, “Go to the Phoenix Pavilion in the rear garden and wait for me there.” Lü Bu went straight there with his halberd and stood beside the curved balustrade beneath the pavilion. After a long while, Diaochan came parting the flowers and brushing past the willows, looking truly like a fairy from the Palace of the Moon. Weeping, she said to Lü Bu, “Though I am not Minister Wang's own daughter, he has treated me as his own flesh and blood. From the moment I met you and was promised the honor of serving you as your wife, my lifelong wish was fulfilled. Who could have imagined that the Grand Preceptor would conceive a wicked desire and violate me? I bitterly regret that I did not die at once. Only because I had not yet bid you a final farewell did I endure the shame and cling to life. Now that I have had the good fortune to see you, my last wish is fulfilled. My body is already defiled, and I can no longer serve a hero. Let me die before you and thereby prove the constancy of my heart!” As soon as she finished speaking, she gripped the curved railing and made to leap into the lotus pond. Lü Bu hastily caught her in his arms and cried, “I have long understood your heart! I have only lamented that we had no chance to speak together!” Diaochan clutched at Lü Bu and said, “If I cannot become your wife in this life, then let us pledge ourselves to meet in the next.” Lü Bu said, “If I cannot make you my wife in this life, I am no hero!” Diaochan said, “Each day seems a year to me. Have pity and save me, my lord.” Lü Bu said, “I slipped away in a moment of leisure. I fear that old villain will grow suspicious, so I must leave at once.” Diaochan seized his robe and said, “If you are so afraid of that old villain, there will never be a day when I see the light of heaven again!” Lü Bu halted and said, “Give me time to devise a sound plan.” With that, he raised his halberd and prepared to leave. Diaochan said, “While secluded in the women's quarters, I heard your fame resounding like thunder and believed you to be the one unrivaled man of this age. Who would have thought that you, too, were subject to another man's will!” When she finished, her tears fell like rain. Lü Bu's face flushed with shame. He leaned his halberd aside once more, turned back, embraced Diaochan, and soothed her with tender words. The two clung close together, unable to bear parting.

p.src: Meanwhile, in the palace, Dong Zhuo turned and saw that Lü Bu was gone. Growing suspicious, he hastily took leave of Emperor Xian, boarded his carriage, and returned to his residence. There he saw Lü Bu's horse tethered before the gate. He questioned the gatekeeper, who replied, “The Marquis of Wen went into the rear hall.” Dong Zhuo ordered his attendants away and went straight into the rear hall, but could not find him. He called for Diaochan, but she too was nowhere to be seen. He urgently questioned a maid, who said, “Diaochan is admiring the flowers in the rear garden.” Dong Zhuo hurried into the rear garden and caught sight of Lü Bu and Diaochan talking together beneath the Phoenix Pavilion, with the painted halberd leaning off to one side. Furious, Dong Zhuo let out a great roar. Seeing Dong Zhuo arrive, Lü Bu was greatly alarmed and turned to flee. Dong Zhuo snatched up the painted halberd and charged after him with it leveled. Lü Bu ran swiftly, while the corpulent Dong Zhuo could not catch him, so Dong Zhuo hurled the halberd at Lü Bu. Lü Bu struck the halberd to the ground. Dong Zhuo picked up the halberd and gave chase again, but Lü Bu was already far away. As Dong Zhuo rushed out through the garden gate, a man came flying toward him and collided squarely with his chest, knocking him to the ground. And so it was:
